newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ample liquidity helps German call money rates dip.
newsitem.headline: Ample liquidity helps German call money rates dip.

text.p: Buffeted by sufficient liquidity, German call money rates dipped further on Thursday, trading level with the Bundesbank's main money market rate.
Overnight funds traded between 3.00/3.02 percent on Thursday with the bulk of trades conducted at 3.00 percent, the Bundesbank's key money market rate, the repo.
This compares with rates of 3.02/3.03 percent seen on Wednesday.
Rates nudged slightly lower in late morning trading when traders were comforted by news reserve holdings at the Bundesbank were rather more ample.

Traders had been nervous this morning as they had no idea about the shape of reserve numbers, as data release was delayed from the Bundesbank after lightning struck one of the regional central banks. The Bundesbank did not specify which bank.

On Wednesday banks held 40.4 billion marks at the Bundesbank, up from 39.6 billion marks held one day earlier. The average monthly rate was set unchanged at 40.4 billion marks. Lombard borrowings were negligible.
As expected the Bundesbank kept its three key interest rates steady, keeping the main money market rate at three percent, the rate that has prevailed for nearly one year.
"The market is clearly quite liquid," said one dealer, noting banks were having a difficult time getting rid of funds.
On the other hand dealers also said they had no expectations for rates to dip much below the three percent level, as they did not feel the Bundesbank would tolerate a dramatic and ongoing decline.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.04333 percent on Thursday compared with 3.0475 percent on Wednesday.
